svg.font-family: 'Roboto Mono', ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, monospace
svg.title: One Volta SM, four schedulers
svg.desc: A Volta SM has an L1 instruction cache on top, four processing blocks each with an L0 instruction cache, one warp scheduler and one dispatch unit at 32 threads per clock, a 64 KB register file, 8 FP64, 16 INT32 and 16 FP32 units, 2 tensor cores, LD/ST units and an SFU, and at the bottom a shared 128 KB L1 data cache and shared memory plus 4 texture units. The side panel shows a kernel grid split into blocks, blocks placed on SMs with free resources, warps of 32 spread over the 4 schedulers, the compute capability 7.0 limits, the tensor core D = A times B plus C on 4 by 4 FP16 tiles, and that V100 has no BF16 or TF32.
svg.text: V100 has 80 of these. Each one juggles up to 64 warps.
a grid of blocks, any order
one block per SM that still has room
shared below them: 128 KB L1, smem up to 96 KB
64 warps and 2048 threads per SM. No BF16 or TF32. Tensor core is D = A × B + C.
